sourceDate.text: 命宋州節度使元行欽率騎三千赴鄴都招撫
丁未，鄴都行營招撫使元行欽率諸道之師再攻鄴都

zh.exact: 鄴都行營招撫使元行欽

units.zh: 李建及，許州人。
units.en: Li Jianji was from Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Li Jianji was a native of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 本姓王，父質。
units.en: His family name had originally been Wang; his father was named Zhi.
units.literal: His original surname was Wang; his father's name was Zhi.

units.zh: 建及少事李罕之為紀綱，光啟中，罕之謁武皇於晉陽，因選部下驍勇者百人以獻，建及在籍中。
units.en: As a young man Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp officer. During the Guangqi reign Hanzhi called on the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and presented a hundred picked warriors from his command; Jianji was among them.
units.literal: In his youth Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp disciplinarian. In the Guangqi era Hanzhi visited the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and, selecting a hundred valiant men from his subordinates to present, Jianji was on the roster.

units.zh: 後以功署牙職，典義兒軍，及賜姓名。
units.en: He later earned appointment to the guard staff, command of the adopted-sons corps, and the gift of a surname and given name.
units.literal: Later, for merit he was appointed to a guard-office post, placed in charge of the adopted-sons army, and granted a surname and personal name.

units.zh: 天祐七年，改匡衛軍都校。
units.en: In the seventh year of Tianyou he was made commandant of the Kuangwei Army.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou he was changed to commandant of the Kuangwei Army.

units.zh: 柏鄉之役，汴將韓追周德威至高邑南野河上，鎮、定兵扼橋道，韓選精兵先奪之。
units.en: At Baixiang the Bian commander Han Zhui pressed Zhou Dewei to the open country south of Gaoyi along the river. The Zhen and Ding forces blocked the bridge approach, and Han sent picked troops to take it first.
units.literal: In the campaign at Baixiang, the Bian general Han Zhui pursued Zhou Dewei to the wilds south of Gaoyi on the river; the Zhen and Ding troops held the bridge road, and Han chose elite troops to seize it first.

units.zh: 莊宗登高而望，鎮、定兵將衄，謂建及曰：「如賊過橋，則勢不可遏，卿計若何？」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong took a vantage point and saw the Zhen and Ding lines buckling. He asked Jianji, "If they get across that bridge we cannot stop them—what do you advise?"
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong climbed high to look; the Zhen and Ding troops were about to be driven back, and he said to Jianji, "If the enemy cross the bridge, their momentum cannot be checked—what is your plan?"

units.zh: 建及於部選士二百，挺槍大噪，禦汴軍，卻之於橋下。
units.en: Jianji picked two hundred men from his command, charged with leveled spears and a thunderous cry, and threw the Bian troops back from the bridge.
units.literal: Jianji from his unit chose two hundred men, levelled spears with a great shout, and met the Bian army, driving them back below the bridge.

units.zh: 二月，王師攻魏，魏人夜出犯我營，建及設伏待之，扼其歸路，盡殪之。
units.en: In the second month the imperial army besieged Wei. Wei forces raided the camp by night; Jianji laid an ambush, cut off their retreat, and wiped them out.
units.literal: In the second month the royal army attacked Wei; the Wei men came out by night to strike our camp. Jianji set an ambush and waited, blocked their return route, and annihilated them.

units.zh: 劉鄩之營莘縣，月餘不出，忽一旦縱兵攻鎮、定之營，軍中騰亂，建及率銀槍勁兵千人赴之，擊敗汴軍，追奔至其壘。
units.en: Liu Yan had camped at Huaxian and for more than a month refused battle, then one day suddenly struck the Zhen and Ding encampment. As the army churned in panic, Jianji rushed up with a thousand silver-spear veterans, routed the Bian force, and chased them to their walls.
units.literal: Liu Yan's camp was at Huaxian; for more than a month he did not come out, then suddenly one day he loosed his troops to attack the Zhen and Ding camp. The army was thrown into uproar; Jianji led a thousand silver-spear crack troops to the spot, defeated the Bian army, and pursued them to their ramparts.

units.zh: 元城之戰，建及首陷其陣，授天雄軍教練使。
units.en: At Yuancheng Jianji led the breach of the enemy line and was made drill instructor of the Tianxiong Army.
units.literal: In the battle of Yuancheng Jianji was first to break their line and was appointed instructor of the Tianxiong Army.

units.zh: 八月，遷遼州刺史。
units.en: In the eighth month he was transferred to the prefecture of Liao.
units.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to be prefect of Liaozhou.

units.zh: 十四年，從擊契丹於幽州，破之。
units.en: In the fourteenth year he joined the campaign against the Khitan at Youzhou and routed them.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the attack on the Khitan at Youzhou and defeated them.

units.zh: 十二月，從攻楊劉，自寅至午，汴軍嬰城拒守，建及自負葭葦堙塹，率先登梯，遂拔之。
units.en: In the twelfth month he took part in the assault on Yangliu. From dawn to midday the Bian garrison held the walls. Jianji carried bundles of reeds to fill the ditch, was first on the scaling ladder, and the city fell.
units.literal: In the twelfth month he followed the assault on Yangliu; from the hour yin to the hour wu the Bian army clung to the walls in defense. Jianji shouldered reed bundles to fill the moat, was first up the ladder, and the place was taken.

units.zh: 胡柳之役，前軍逗撓，際晚，汴軍登土山，建及一戰奪之。
units.en: At Huliu the forward units stalled. Toward dusk the Bian troops seized a hillock; Jianji retook it in a single clash.
units.literal: In the battle of Huliu the vanguard hung back; toward evening the Bian army climbed an earthen hill, and Jianji in one fight wrested it from them.

units.zh: 莊宗欲收軍，詰朝合戰。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong wanted to pull the army back and fight again at dawn.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong wished to withdraw the army and join battle at dawn the next day.

units.zh: 建及橫槊當前，曰：「賊大將已亡，乘此易擊，王但登山，觀臣破賊！」
units.en: Jianji planted his spear in their path and said, "Their chief commander is already dead—this is the moment to hit them while they are easy prey. Your Majesty has only to take the hill and watch me smash the foe!"
units.literal: Jianji set his spear across the front and said, "The enemy's great general is already dead; press this advantage while it is easy to strike. Your Majesty need only climb the hill and watch your servant break the enemy!"

units.zh: 即引銀槍效節大呼奮擊，三軍增氣，由是王師復振，以功授檢校司空、魏博內外衙都將。
units.en: He immediately led the silver-spear Xiaojie guard in a roaring charge; morale surged through the army, and the imperial force rallied. For this he received the acting title of Sikong and command of Weibo's inner and outer gate troops.
units.literal: At once he led the silver-spear Xiaojie troops in a great shout and fierce attack; the three armies took heart, and thereby the royal army revived. For merit he was appointed acting Sikong and commander of the inner and outer gates of Weibo.

units.zh: 十六年，汴將賀瑰攻德勝南城，以戰船十餘艘，竹笮維之，扼斷津路，王師不得渡。
units.en: In the sixteenth year the Bian commander He Gui assaulted the southern quarter of Desheng with a dozen warships roped together with bamboo hawsers, blocking the crossing and keeping the imperial army on the far bank.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year the Bian general He Gui attacked the southern city of Desheng with more than ten war junks linked by bamboo chains, cutting the ford and preventing the royal army from crossing.

units.zh: 城中矢石將盡，守城將氏延賞危急，莊宗令積帛軍門，召能破賊船者。
units.en: Missiles and stones inside the walls were almost gone, and the defender Shi Yanzhang was at the breaking point. Emperor Zhuangzong heaped silk at the camp gate and offered it to anyone who could destroy the enemy fleet.
units.literal: Arrows and stones in the city were nearly exhausted; the defending general Shi Yanzhang was in desperate straits. The Emperor Zhuangzong had silk piled at the army gate and called for whoever could break the enemy ships.

units.zh: 津人有馬破龍者，能水遊，乃令往見延賞，延賞言：「危窘極矣，所爭晷刻。」
units.en: A local swimmer named Ma Polong was sent in to Yanzhang, who told him, "We are at the very edge—every instant counts."
units.literal: A man of the ford district named Ma Polong, who could swim, was sent to see Yanzhang. Yanzhang said, "The peril is extreme; what we contest is a matter of moments."

units.zh: 時棹船滿河，流矢雨集，建及被重鎧，執槊呼曰：「豈有一衣帶水，縱賊如此！」
units.en: The river was thick with boats and arrows fell in sheets. Jianji in heavy mail gripped his spear and cried, "Is it only a strip of water wide, and we still let the enemy have their way?"
units.literal: At that time oared boats filled the river and arrows fell like rain. Jianji wore heavy armor, grasped his spear, and shouted, "Can there be only a belt of water and yet we let the enemy run wild like this!"

units.zh: 乃以二船實甲士，皆短兵持斧，徑抵梁之戰艦，斧其笮；
units.en: He sent two boats packed with armored men armed with short weapons and axes straight at the Liang warships and cut through the bamboo hawsers.
units.literal: Then with two boats loaded with armored men, all bearing short weapons and axes, he went straight at the Liang war junks and chopped through the bamboo chains.

units.zh: 又令上流具甕，積薪其上，順流縱火，以攻其艦。
units.en: He also had men upstream ready earthen jars piled with kindling, set them afire, and floated them down against the fleet.
units.literal: He also ordered men upstream to prepare jars and pile fuel on them, then sent them downstream ablaze to attack the junks.

units.zh: 須臾，煙焰騰熾，梁軍斷纜而遁；
units.en: Within moments smoke and flame towered up; the Liang crews cut their moorings and fled.
units.literal: In an instant smoke and flame rose fiercely; the Liang army cut their cables and fled.

units.zh: 建及乃入南城，賀瑰解圍而去。
units.en: Jianji then entered the southern city, and He Gui broke off the siege and withdrew.
units.literal: Jianji then entered the southern city, and He Gui lifted the siege and withdrew.

units.zh: 其年十二月，與汴將王瓚戰於戚城，建及傷手，莊宗解禦衣金帶賜之。
units.en: That twelfth month he fought the Bian commander Wang Zan at Qicheng. Jianji took a wound to the hand, and Emperor Zhuangzong took off his own court robe and gold belt and gave them to him.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he fought the Bian general Wang Zan at Qicheng; Jianji was wounded in the hand, and the Emperor Zhuangzong removed his own imperial robe and gold belt and bestowed them on him.

units.zh: 建及有膽氣，慷慨不群，臨陣鞠旅，意氣橫壯，自莊宗至魏州，建及都總內外衙銀槍效節帳前親軍，善於撫禦，所得賞賜，皆分給部下，絕甘分少，頗洽軍情。
units.en: Jianji was bold and high-spirited, generous and unlike ordinary men. On the battlefield his bearing was formidable. From Zhuangzong's arrival in Weizhou onward he commanded the silver-spear Xiaojie guard of the inner and outer gates and knew how to win soldiers' hearts. Every reward he shared with his men, refusing the choicest portion and taking the least—so he held the army's loyalty.
units.literal: Jianji had courage and an open, generous spirit, uncommon among men. When he arrayed troops on the field his spirit was towering. From the time the Emperor Zhuangzong reached Weizhou, Jianji had overall command of the inner and outer gate silver-spear Xiaojie guard before the imperial tent; he was skilled at comforting and controlling them. Whatever rewards he received he divided among his subordinates, keeping none of the best for himself and taking the smallest share—thus he won the army's affection.

units.zh: 又累立戰功，雄勇冠絕，雌劣者忌讒之。
units.en: He piled up victories and had no peer in bravery, and lesser men nursed envy and whispered against him.
units.literal: He also repeatedly won battle merit and stood alone in valor; the weak and petty envied and slandered him.

units.zh: 時宦官韋令圖監建及軍，每於莊宗前言：「建及以家財驟施，其趨向誌意不小，不可令典衙兵。」
units.en: The eunuch Wei Lingtu was then overseeing Jianji's command and kept telling Zhuangzong, "Jianji is throwing his family fortune around in sudden largesse; his ambitions are larger than they look—he must not be left in charge of the gate army."
units.literal: At that time the eunuch Wei Lingtu supervised Jianji's army and repeatedly said before the Emperor Zhuangzong, "Jianji suddenly dispenses his family wealth; his aims and ambitions are no small matter—he must not be allowed to command the gate troops."

units.zh: 莊宗因猜之。
units.en: Zhuangzong took the hint and began to distrust him.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong therefore grew suspicious of him.

units.zh: 建及性既忠藎，雖知讒構，不改其操。
units.en: Jianji was by nature steadfast and loyal; even when he knew men were weaving plots against him, he did not change how he served.
units.literal: Jianji's nature was loyal and earnest; though he knew of the slander and plotting, he did not alter his conduct.

units.zh: 十七年三月，授代州刺史。
units.en: In the third month of the seventeenth year he was made prefect of Dai.
units.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year he was appointed prefect of Daizhou.

units.zh: 八月，與李存審赴河中，解同州之圍。
units.en: In the eighth month he marched with Li Cunshen to Hezhong and raised the siege of Tong.
units.literal: In the eighth month he went with Li Cunshen to the Hezhong region and lifted the siege of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 建及少遇禍亂，久從戰陣，矢石所中，肌無完膚，後有功見疑，私心憤鬱。
units.en: He had grown up in chaos and spent his life in the field; arrow and stone had left scarcely an unmarked inch of skin. When merit only brought suspicion, he nursed a private bitterness.
units.literal: Jianji in his youth had met with calamity and disorder and long followed the battle line; wherever arrows and stones struck, no patch of flesh on him remained whole. Later, though he had merit, he was met with suspicion, and in private he brooded in anger and grief.

units.zh: 是歲，卒於太原，時年五十七。
units.en: That year he died at Taiyuan, at the age of fifty-seven.
units.literal: That year he died at Taiyuan, aged fifty-seven.

units.zh: 石君立，趙州昭慶人也，亦謂之石家財。
units.en: Shi Junli came from Zhaqing in Zhao Prefecture and was also known as Shi Jiacai.
units.literal: Shi Junli was a native of Zhao Prefecture, Zhaqing district; he was also called Shi Jiacai.

units.zh: 初事代州刺史李克柔，後隸李嗣昭為牙校，曆典諸軍。
units.en: He first served Li Kerou, prefect of Dai, then entered Li Sizhao's guard and rose through commands over several armies.
units.literal: At first he served the Daizhou prefect Li Kerou; later he came under Li Sizhao as a guard officer and successively held command of various armies.

units.zh: 夾城之役，君立每出挑戰，壞汴軍柵壘，俘擒而還。
units.en: At Jiacheng he repeatedly rode out to challenge the foe, tore up Bian stockades and walls, and came back with prisoners.
units.literal: In the campaign at Jiacheng Junli each time went out to challenge the enemy, destroyed Bian palisades and ramparts, and returned with captives.

units.zh: 八年，與汴軍戰於龍化園，敗之，獲其大將卜渥以獻。
units.en: In the eighth year he met the Bian army at Longhua Garden, routed them, and sent up their commander Bu Wo as a captive.
units.literal: In the eighth year he fought the Bian army at Longhua Garden, defeated them, and presented their great general Bu Wo as captive.

units.zh: 嗣昭每出征，俾君立為前鋒，敵人畏之。
units.en: Whenever Sizhao took the field he put Junli in the van, and enemies learned to dread the name.
units.literal: Whenever Sizhao went on campaign he made Junli his vanguard; the enemy feared him.

units.zh: 王檀之逼晉陽也，城中無備，安金全驅市人以登陴，保聚不完。
units.en: When Wang Tan closed on Taiyuan the city was unprepared. An Jinquan pressed townsfolk onto the ramparts, but the defenses were still patchwork.
units.literal: When Wang Tan pressed on Taiyuan the city had no preparations; An Jinquan drove townspeople onto the walls, but the defenses were incomplete.

units.zh: 時莊宗在魏博，救應不暇，人心危懼，嗣昭遣君立率五百騎，自上黨朝發暮至。
units.en: Zhuangzong was in Weibo and could not break away to help; panic spread. Sizhao dispatched Junli with five hundred cavalry from Shangdang—they left at dawn and reached Taiyuan by nightfall.
units.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong was then in Weibo and could not spare relief; hearts were fearful. Sizhao sent Junli with five hundred horsemen, who set out from Shangdang at dawn and arrived at dusk.

units.zh: 王檀遊軍扼汾橋，君立一戰敗之，徑至城下，馳突斬擊，出入如神，大呼曰：「昭義侍中大軍至矣！」
units.en: Wang Tan's scouts held the Fen Bridge; Junli smashed them in one clash, raced to the wall, and wheeled through the Bian ranks like a force of nature, roaring, "The Grand Preceptor of Zhaoyi is here with the main host!"
units.literal: Wang Tan's roaming detachments held the Fen Bridge; Junli defeated them in one fight, went straight to the foot of the wall, and charged in and out like a spirit, shouting loudly, "The Grand Preceptor of Zhaoyi has arrived with the great army!"

units.zh: 是夜入城，與安金全等分出諸門擊殺於外，遲明，梁軍敗走。
units.en: He entered the city that night. With An Jinquan and others he sent parties out every gate to cut down the enemy outside; by first light the Liang army broke and ran.
units.literal: That night he entered the city; with An Jinquan and others he sent men out through the various gates to strike and kill outside. At the light of dawn the Liang army was defeated and fled.

units.zh: 十七年，將兵屯德勝。
units.en: In the seventeenth year he garrisoned Desheng with his troops.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he led troops to garrison Desheng.

units.zh: 時汴軍自滑州轉餉以給楊村寨，莊宗親率騎軍於河外，循岸而上，邀擊之。
units.en: The Bian forces were shipping grain from Huazhou to Yangcun village; Zhuangzong himself led cavalry along the north bank upstream to intercept the convoys.
units.literal: At that time the Bian army turned supplies from Huazhou to feed the stockade at Yangcun; the Emperor Zhuangzong personally led cavalry along the riverbank upstream to intercept them.

units.zh: 汴人距楊村五十里，於河曲潘張村築壘以貯軍儲，莊宗令諸軍攻之。
units.en: Fifty li short of Yangcun the enemy threw up a depot at Panzhang Village in the river bend; Zhuangzong ordered a general assault.
units.literal: The Bian men, fifty li from Yangcun, built a stockade at Panzhang Village on the river bend to store provisions, and the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the armies to attack it.

units.zh: 汴人設伏於要路，逆戰偽敗，王師乘之，蹙入壘門，梁伏兵起，因與血戰。
units.en: The Bian laid an ambush on the approach, offered a sham retreat, and drew the imperial troops charging through the gate. Liang men hidden inside sprang up and a savage melee followed.
units.literal: The Bian men set an ambush on the critical road, met them in battle with a feigned defeat; the royal army pressed the pursuit and was crowded into the stockade gate. Liang hidden troops rose, and a bloody fight ensued.

units.zh: 君立與鎮州大將王釗陷入賊壘，時諸將部校陷賊者十餘人，君立被執，送於汴。
units.en: Junli and the Zhen commander Wang Zhao were caught inside the enemy fort along with more than a dozen other officers. Junli was taken and sent to Bian.
units.literal: Junli and the Zhenzhou great general Wang Zhao fell into the enemy stockade; at the time more than ten generals and officers of various commands were trapped in the enemy works. Junli was seized and sent to Bian.

units.zh: 梁祖素知其驍勇，欲用之為將，械而下獄。
units.en: The Liang founder had long admired his fighting name and wanted him as a commander; they shackled him and threw him in prison.
units.literal: The Liang Founder had long known his valor and wished to use him as a general; he was put in fetters and cast into prison.

units.zh: 久之，梁主遣人誘之，君立曰：「敗軍之將，難與議勇，如欲將我，我雖真誠效命，能信我乎？
units.en: After a long interval the Liang ruler sent envoys to win him over. Junli answered, "A beaten general is no one to talk bravery with. Even if I meant every word of loyalty, would you believe me?
units.literal: After a long while the Liang ruler sent men to entice him. Junli said, "A defeated commander is a poor man to discuss valor with. If you wish to employ me, though I would serve you in all sincerity, could you trust me?

units.zh: 人皆有君，吾何忍反為仇人哉！」
units.en: Every man already has his sovereign—how could I stomach serving the man who is my foe?"
units.literal: Every man has his lord—how could I bear to turn and serve my enemy?"

units.zh: 既而諸將被戮，尚惜君立不之害。
units.en: Before long the other captured officers were put to death, but they still kept Junli alive.
units.literal: Soon after, the other captured generals were executed, yet they still spared Junli and did not kill him.

units.zh: 同光元年，莊宗至汴前一日，梁主始令殺之。
units.en: In the first year of Tongguang, the day before Zhuangzong entered Bian, the Liang ruler finally had him executed.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongguang, on the day before the Emperor Zhuangzong reached Bian, the Liang ruler at last ordered him killed.

units.zh: 高行珪，燕人也。
units.en: Gao Xinggui was a native of Yan.
units.literal: Gao Xinggui was a man of Yan.

units.zh: 家世勇悍，與弟行周俱有武藝，初仕燕為騎將，驍果出諸將之右。
units.en: The Gaos were a fighting clan for generations; he and his younger brother Xingzhou were both skilled in arms. They first served Yan as cavalry officers and stood out even among Yan's hardiest commanders.
units.literal: His family for generations had been fierce and martial; he and his younger brother Xingzhou both had military skill. At first they served Yan as cavalry officers, bold and resolute above the other generals.

units.zh: 燕帥劉守光僭逆不道，莊宗令周德威征之，守光大懼，以行珪為武州刺史，令張犄角之勢。
units.en: When the Yan warlord Liu Shouguang seized power unlawfully, Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei against him. Shouguang in alarm made Xinggui prefect of Wu and set him to brace the frontier.
units.literal: The Yan commander Liu Shouguang was rebellious and lawless; the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Zhou Dewei to campaign against him. Shouguang was greatly afraid and appointed Xinggui prefect of Wu, ordering him to spread horns in mutual support.

units.zh: 時明宗將兵助德威平燕，俄聞行珪至，率騎以禦之。
units.en: Mingzong was then assisting Dewei in the Yan campaign; when word came that Xinggui was advancing, he rode out to confront him.
units.literal: At that time the Emperor Mingzong was leading troops to help Dewei pacify Yan; soon word came that Xinggui had arrived, and he led cavalry to meet him.

units.zh: 明宗諭以逆順之理，行珪乃降。
units.en: Mingzong laid out the difference between rebellion and rightful service, and Xinggui submitted.
units.literal: The Emperor Mingzong explained the logic of loyalty and rebellion, and Xinggui thereupon surrendered.

units.zh: 守光將元行欽在山北，聞行珪有變，即率部下軍眾以攻行珪。
units.en: Shouguang's officer Yuan Xingqin was in the northern hills; when he heard Xinggui had turned, he marched at once with his troops to attack him.
units.literal: Shouguang's general Yuan Xingqin was north of the mountains; hearing that Xinggui had changed sides, he at once led his subordinates and army masses to attack Xinggui.

units.zh: 行珪遣弟行周告急於周德威，德威命明宗、李嗣本、安金全將兵援之。
units.en: Xinggui sent Xingzhou in haste to Zhou Dewei; Dewei ordered Mingzong, Li Siben, and An Jinquan to march to his relief.
units.literal: Xinggui sent his younger brother Xingzhou in haste to Zhou Dewei to report the emergency; Dewei ordered the Emperor Mingzong, Li Siben, and An Jinquan to lead troops to relieve him.

units.zh: 明宗破行欽於廣邊軍，行欽亦降。
units.en: Mingzong routed Xingqin at Guangbian and took his surrender as well.
units.literal: The Emperor Mingzong defeated Xingqin at Guangbian Army, and Xingqin also surrendered.

units.zh: 尋以行珪為朔州刺史，曆忻、嵐二郡，遷雲州留後。
units.en: He was soon made prefect of Shuo, then served Xin and Lan in turn, and was promoted to acting military commissioner of Yun.
units.literal: Soon after, Xinggui was made prefect of Shuo, successively held Xin and Lan prefectures, and was transferred to be acting military commissioner of Yun.

units.zh: 天成初，授鄧州節度使，尋移鎮安州。
units.en: At the opening of the Tiancheng era he was made military commissioner of Deng, then shifted to An.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of Dengzhou; soon after he was transferred to garrison Anzhou.

units.zh: 行珪性貪鄙，短於為政，在安州日，行事多不法。
units.en: Xinggui was grasping and coarse, a poor administrator; at An his rule was repeatedly outside the law.
units.literal: Xinggui was greedy and base, deficient in governing; in his days at Anzhou his conduct was often unlawful.

units.zh: 副使範延策者，幽州人也，性剛直，累為賓職，及佐行珪，睹其貪猥，因強諫之，行珪不從。
units.en: His deputy Fan Yanji came from Youzhou, blunt and upright, and had served many lords as staff officer. Under Xinggui he saw the corruption and pressed him hard in counsel, but Xinggui would not listen.
units.literal: His vice commissioner Fan Yanji was a man of Youzhou, by nature upright and blunt; he had repeatedly served in staff posts, and when he assisted Xinggui he witnessed his greed and vileness and therefore remonstrated forcefully, but Xinggui would not heed him.

units.zh: 後延策因入奏，獻封章於闕下，事有三條：一請不禁過淮豬羊，而禁絲綿匹帛，以實中國；
units.en: Later Yanji went to court and filed a memorial at the palace with three proposals: first, stop banning pigs and sheep south of the Huai but ban silk and cotton instead, to strengthen the heartland;
units.literal: Later Yanji entered court to report and submitted a memorial at the palace gate with three items: first, that they should not forbid pigs and sheep crossing the Huai but should forbid silk and cotton cloth, to enrich the central state;

units.zh: 一請於山林要害置軍鎮，以絕寇盜；
units.en: second, post garrisons at mountain passes and forests to choke off banditry;
units.literal: second, that they should place military garrisons at strategic points in mountains and forests to cut off bandits and robbers;

units.zh: 一述藩侯之弊，請敕從事明諫諍之，不從，令諸軍校列班廷諍。
units.en: third, describe the abuses of regional commanders and order their staffs to speak plainly, and if they would not, require their officers to remonstrate in open court.
units.literal: third, that he set forth the abuses of frontier lords and asked that the throne order staff to remonstrate clearly, and if they would not, order military officers to line up in court and remonstrate.

units.zh: 行珪聞之，深銜之。
units.en: When Xinggui heard of the memorial he hated Fan Yanji bitterly.
units.literal: When Xinggui heard of it he deeply resented him.

units.zh: 後因戍兵作亂，誣奏延策與之同謀，父子俱戮於汴，聞者冤之。
units.en: Later, when garrison troops mutinied, he falsely accused Yanji of complicity; father and son were both executed at Bian, and public opinion called it a gross injustice.
units.literal: Later, because garrison soldiers mutinied, he falsely memorialized that Yanji had plotted with them, and father and son were both executed at Bian; those who heard of it deemed it a grievous wrong.

units.zh: 未幾，行珪以疾卒。
units.en: Not long after, Xinggui died of illness.
units.literal: Before long Xinggui died of illness.

units.zh: 詔贈太尉。
units.en: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 張廷裕，代北人也。
units.en: Zhang Tingyu came from the northern frontier of Dai.
units.literal: Zhang Tingyu was a man of the northern Dai region.

units.zh: 幼事武皇於雲中，從平黃巢，討王行瑜，自行間漸升為小將。
units.en: As a youth he served the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong, followed him against Huang Chao and Wang Xingyu, and slowly rose from the ranks to junior command.
units.literal: In his youth he served the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong; he followed in the pacification of Huang Chao and the campaign against Wang Xingyu and gradually rose from the ranks to become a junior general.

units.zh: 莊宗定魏，補天雄軍左廂馬步都虞候，曆蔚、慈、隰三州刺史。
units.en: When Zhuangzong secured Wei he was made left-wing horse-and-foot commandant of the Tianxiong Army and later held the prefectures of Wei, Ci, and Xi in succession.
units.literal: When the Emperor Zhuangzong settled Wei he was appointed left-wing horse-and-foot commandant of the Tianxiong Army and successively served as prefect of Wei, Ci, and Xi.

units.zh: 同光三年，除新州節度使。
units.en: In the third year of Tongguang he was appointed military commissioner of Xin.
units.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was made military commissioner of Xinzhou.

units.zh: 塞上多事，廷裕無控製之術，邊鄙常聳。
units.en: The northern marches were in constant turmoil; Tingyu lacked the skill to hold them, and the frontier stayed on edge.
units.literal: The frontier was troubled with many affairs; Tingyu had no art of control, and the borderlands were often alarmed.

units.zh: 天成三年，卒於治所。
units.en: In the third year of Tiancheng he died in office.
units.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at his headquarters.

units.zh: 詔贈太保。
units.en: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.
units.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 王思同，幽州人也。
units.en: Wang Sitong was a native of Youzhou.
units.literal: Wang Sitong was a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 父敬柔，曆瀛、平、儒、檀、營五州刺史。
units.en: His father Jingrou had been prefect in turn of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and a second Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: His father Jingrou successively served as prefect of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and Ying prefectures.

units.zh: 思同母即劉仁恭之女也，故思同初事仁恭為帳下軍校。
units.en: Sitong's mother was a daughter of Liu Rengong, so he first served Rengong as an officer in his personal guard.
units.literal: Sitong's mother was a daughter of Liu Rengong; therefore Sitong at first served Rengong as a guard officer under his tent.

units.zh: 會劉守光攻仁恭於大安山，思同以部下兵歸太原，時年十六，武皇命為飛騰指揮使。
units.en: When Liu Shouguang besieged Rengong at Mount Da'an, Sitong brought his men over to Taiyuan. He was sixteen; the Martial Emperor made him commander of the Feiteng guard.
units.literal: When Liu Shouguang attacked Rengong at Da'an Mountain, Sitong led his subordinate troops to Taiyuan; he was then sixteen, and the Martial Emperor appointed him commander of the Feiteng guard.

units.zh: 從莊宗平定山東，累典諸軍。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong in the pacification of Shandong and held a series of army commands.
units.literal: He followed the Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong and successively held command of various armies.

units.zh: 思同性疏俊，粗有文，性喜為詩什，與人唱和，自稱薊門戰客。
units.en: Sitong was easy in manner and not without book learning; he loved to write verse, traded poems with friends, and called himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.
units.literal: Sitong was by nature open and handsome, had some learning in letters, delighted in composing verse, exchanged poems with others, and styled himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.

units.zh: 魏王繼岌待之若子。
units.en: The Prince of Wei, Jiji, treated him almost as a son.
units.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji treated him like a son.

units.zh: 時內養呂知柔侍興聖宮，頗用事，思同不平之。
units.en: The palace eunuch Lü Zhirou, who served the Xingsheng Palace, had grown powerful; Sitong chafed at it.
units.literal: At that time the inner attendant Lü Zhirou attended the Xingsheng Palace and wielded considerable power; Sitong resented this.

units.zh: 呂為終南山詩，末句有「頭」字，思同和曰：「料伊直擬衝霄漢，賴有青天壓著頭。」
units.en: Lü wrote a poem on Mount Zhongnan ending with the word "head"; Sitong answered, "You seem ready to punch through the sky—lucky for you the blue heaven still weighs on your head."
units.literal: Lü composed a poem on Mount Zhongnan whose closing line contained the character "head"; Sitong replied in verse, "I suppose you mean to pierce the heavens—fortunately blue heaven still presses on your head."

units.zh: 其所為詩句，皆此類也。
units.en: His verses were all barbs of that kind.
units.literal: The lines he wrote in his poems were all of this sort.

units.zh: 每從征，必在興聖帳下，然同光朝，位止鄭州刺史。
units.en: He campaigned always in the Xingsheng train, yet under Tongguang he rose no higher than prefect of Zheng.
units.literal: Whenever he followed on campaign he was always under the Xingsheng tent, yet in the Tongguang reign his rank stopped at prefect of Zheng.

units.zh: 明宗在軍時，素知之，即位後，用為同州節度使，未幾，移鎮隴右。
units.en: Mingzong had known him in the field; once enthroned he made him commissioner of Tong, then soon moved him to Longyou.
units.literal: The Emperor Mingzong had known him well when in the army; after he took the throne he used him as military commissioner of Tongzhou, and before long transferred him to garrison Longyou.

units.zh: 思同好文士，無賢不肖，必館接賄遺，歲費數十萬。
units.en: Sitong cultivated scholars high and low, housed them and showered gifts until he spent hundreds of thousands each year.
units.literal: Sitong favored literary men; whether worthy or base he would lodge and entertain them with gifts, spending several hundred thousand a year.

units.zh: 在秦州累年，邊民懷惠，華戎寧息。
units.en: Through long years at Qin the frontier people felt his kindness, and Chinese and tribesmen alike kept the peace.
units.literal: For many years at Qinzhou the border people cherished his kindness, and Chinese and barbarians were at peace.

units.zh: 長興元年，入朝，見於中興殿。
units.en: In the first year of Changxing he came to court and was received in the Zhongxing Hall.
units.literal: In the first year of Changxing he entered court and was received at the Zhongxing Hall.

units.zh: 明宗問秦州邊事，對曰：「秦州與吐蕃接境，蕃部多違法度。
units.en: Mingzong asked about the Qin frontier. He answered, "Qin marches on Tibet, and many tribesmen ignore our laws.
units.literal: The Emperor Mingzong asked about Qinzhou frontier affairs; he replied, "Qinzhou borders the Tibetans, and many of the tribal peoples violate the law.

units.zh: 臣設法招懷，沿邊置寨四十餘所，控其要害。
units.en: I devised ways to win them and strung more than forty stockades along the border to hold the passes.
units.literal: I devised measures to win them over and along the border set up more than forty stockades to control the strategic points.

units.zh: 每蕃人互市、飲食之界上，令納器械。」
units.en: Whenever Tibetans came to market or ate at the border markets, I required them to hand over their arms."
units.literal: Whenever Tibetans met to trade or took food at the border, I had them surrender their weapons."

units.zh: 因手指畫秦州山川要害控扼處。
units.en: As he spoke he traced with his finger the mountains, rivers, and choke points of Qin on the map.
units.literal: Thereupon with his finger he traced on the map the mountains, rivers, strategic points, and points of control at Qinzhou.

units.zh: 明宗曰：「人言思同不管事，豈及此耶！」
units.en: Mingzong said, "They say Sitong never tends to business—yet look at this!"
units.literal: The Emperor Mingzong said, "People say Sitong pays no attention to affairs—could it reach even to this!"

units.zh: 時兩川叛，欲用之，且留左右，故授右武衛將軍。
units.en: With both Sichuan circuits in revolt the court wanted his service but also wanted him close, so they made him General of the Right Martial Guard.
units.literal: At that time the two Sichuan circuits were in rebellion; they wished to use him but also keep him at court, and therefore appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.

units.zh: 八月，授西南面行營馬步都虞候。
units.en: In the eighth month he was named horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern expedition.
units.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern campaign army.

units.zh: 九月，遷京兆尹、西京留守。
units.en: In the ninth month he became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.
units.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.

units.zh: 伐蜀之役，為先鋒指揮使。
units.en: In the Shu campaign he commanded the vanguard.
units.literal: In the campaign against Shu he served as vanguard commander.

units.zh: 石敬瑭入大散關。
units.en: Shi Jingtang pushed through Dasan Pass.
units.literal: Shi Jingtang entered Dasan Pass.

units.zh: 思同恃勇先入劍門，大軍未相繼，復被董璋兵逐出之。
units.en: Sitong, trusting his bravery, rushed into Jianmen before the main host could follow and was thrown back out by Dong Zhang's men.
units.literal: Sitong, relying on his valor, entered Jianmen first; the main army had not followed in succession, and he was again driven out by Dong Zhang's troops.

units.zh: 及敬瑭班師，思同以曾獲劍門之功，移鎮山南西道。
units.en: When Jingtang pulled the army back, Sitong was shifted to Shannan West Circuit for his earlier success at Jianmen.
units.literal: When Jingtang withdrew the army, Sitong for his former merit in taking Jianmen was transferred to garrison Shannan West Circuit.

units.zh: 三年，兩川交兵，明宗慮並在一人，則朝廷難製，密詔思同相度形勢，即乘間用軍，事未行而董璋敗。
units.en: In the third year the two Sichuan warlords fought each other. Mingzong feared that if one man held both circuits the court could not restrain him, and secretly told Sitong to survey the ground and strike when a chance opened. Before the plan moved, Dong Zhang was already beaten.
units.literal: In the third year the two Sichuan circuits fought each other; the Emperor Mingzong feared that if they were united in one man the court could not control them, and secretly ordered Sitong to assess the situation and seize an opening to use troops. The affair had not been carried out when Dong Zhang was defeated.

units.zh: 八月，復為京兆尹兼西京留守。
units.en: In the eighth month he again took Jingzhao and the western capital in tandem.
units.literal: In the eighth month he was again made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and concurrent custodian of the western capital.

units.zh: 時潞王鎮鳳翔，與之鄰境，及潞王不稟朝旨，致書於秦、涇、雍、梁、邠諸帥，言：「賊臣亂政，屬先帝疾篤，謀害秦王，迎立嗣君，自擅權柄，以致殘害骨肉，搖動藩垣。
units.en: The Prince of Lu held Fengxiang on Sitong's border. When he defied the court he wrote the governors of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin: "Wicked ministers have thrown the government into chaos. As the late emperor lay dying they plotted against the Prince of Qin, installed a puppet heir, and seized power for themselves, wounding the imperial family and unsettling the frontiers.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Lu garrisoned Fengxiang, neighboring his territory; when the Prince of Lu did not obey court orders he sent letters to the commanders of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin, stating, "Traitorous ministers have disorderly government; when the late emperor was gravely ill they plotted to harm the Prince of Qin, welcomed and set up the heir, and on their own grasped power, causing harm to the imperial kin and shaking the frontier screens.

units.zh: 懼先人基業，忽焉墜地，故誓心入朝，以除君側，事濟之後，謝病歸藩。
units.en: I feared our forefathers' legacy would crumble overnight, so I swore to march to court and cut down the men at the emperor's side. Once the work is done I will plead illness and return to my fief.
units.literal: I feared that the forefathers' foundation might suddenly fall to earth; therefore I pledged my heart to enter court to remove those beside the ruler. When the affair is settled I will take leave for illness and return to my fief.

units.zh: 然藩邸素貧。
units.en: Yet the prince's household has always been poor.
units.literal: Yet the princely establishment has always been poor.

units.zh: 兵力俱困，欲希國士，共濟急難。」
units.en: Our forces are spent; we ask the empire's loyal soldiers to help us through the crisis."
units.literal: Our military strength is all exhausted; we wish to look to the state's warriors to share in relieving the urgent difficulty."

units.zh: 乃令小伶女十人以五弦技見思同，因歡諷動，又令軍校宋審溫者，請使於雍，若不從命，即獨圖之。
units.en: He sent ten young women skilled on the five-string zither to perform for Sitong, stirring him with song and mockery, and dispatched the officer Song Shenwen to Yong with an ultimatum: obey, or he would act alone.
units.literal: Thereupon he sent ten young female entertainers skilled on the five-string lute to appear before Sitong and move him with song and satire; he also sent the military officer Song Shenwen to ask leave to go to Yong, saying that if they did not obey the order he would act alone.

units.zh: 又令推官郝昭、府吏朱延乂以書檄起兵。
units.en: He also ordered his staff officer Hao Zhao and clerk Zhu Yanyi to raise troops by proclamation.
units.literal: He further ordered the staff officer Hao Zhao and the clerical official Zhu Yanyi to raise troops with written proclamations.

units.zh: 會副部署藥彥稠至，方宴，而妓、使適至，乃擊之於獄。
units.en: Deputy commander Yao Yanchou arrived during a feast just as the entertainers and envoy appeared; Sitong had them beaten and thrown in jail.
units.literal: When the deputy commander Yao Yanchou arrived they were just at a banquet, and the entertainers and envoy happened to arrive; Sitong had them beaten and cast into prison.

units.zh: 彥稠請誅審溫，拘送昭赴闕。
units.en: Yanchou urged that Shenwen be executed and Zhao sent to the capital in chains.
units.literal: Yanchou asked that Shenwen be executed and Zhao arrested and sent to court.

units.zh: 時思同已遣其子入朝言事，朝廷嘉之，乃以思同為鳳翔行營都部署，起軍營於扶風。
units.en: Sitong had already sent his son to court with a loyal report; the throne commended him and made him overall commander against Fengxiang, encamping the army at Fufeng.
units.literal: At that time Sitong had already sent his son to court to report affairs; the court praised this and therefore made Sitong overall commander of the Fengxiang campaign army, raising the army camp at Fufeng.

units.zh: 三月十四日，與張虔釗會於岐下，梯衝大集。
units.en: On the fourteenth of the third month he joined Zhang Qianjie below Qi; siege ladders and rams crowded the field.
units.literal: On the fourteenth day of the third month he joined Zhang Qianjie at the foot of Qi; scaling ladders and battering rams were massed in great numbers.

units.zh: 十五日，進收東西關城，城中戰備不完，然死力禦捍，外兵傷夷者十二三。
units.en: On the fifteenth they seized the eastern and western gate towns. The city was ill prepared, yet the garrison fought to the last; one or two soldiers in ten of the besiegers were hit.
units.literal: On the fifteenth they advanced to take the eastern and western gate cities; preparations for battle in the city were incomplete, yet the defenders fought to the death to hold them off, and of the outer army one or two in ten were wounded.

units.zh: 十六日，復進攻其城，潞王登陴泣諭於外，聞者悲之。
units.en: On the sixteenth they assaulted the main wall again. The Prince of Lu mounted the ramparts and wept down to the army below; men who heard him were heartsick.
units.literal: On the sixteenth they again pressed the attack on the city; the Prince of Lu climbed the walls and wept as he exhorted those outside, and those who heard were sorrowful.

units.zh: 張虔釗性褊，詰旦，西南用軍，與都監皆血刃以督軍士，軍士齊詬，反攻虔釗，虔釗躍馬避之。
units.en: Zhang Qianjie was hot-tempered. At dawn he threw troops at the southwest corner and, with every inspector, drew steel to drive the men forward. The soldiers cursed him in chorus and turned on him; he spurred his horse away.
units.literal: Zhang Qianjie was narrow by nature; at dawn he used troops on the southwest and with the army inspectors all drew blades to urge on the soldiers. The soldiers cursed together and turned to attack Qianjie, who leaped his horse to escape.

units.zh: 時羽林指揮使楊思權引軍自西門先入，思同未之知，猶督士登城。
units.en: Imperial-guard commander Yang Siquan had already slipped in through the west gate. Sitong knew nothing of it and still drove his men up the ladders.
units.literal: At that time the imperial-guard commander Yang Siquan led troops in first from the west gate; Sitong did not know it and still urged his men up the wall.

units.zh: 俄而嚴衛指揮使尹暉呼曰：「西城軍已入城受賞矣，軍士可解甲！」
units.en: Soon Yin Hui of the strict guard shouted, "The men from the west gate are already inside taking their reward—drop your arms!"
units.literal: Before long the strict-guard commander Yin Hui shouted, "The western-city army has already entered the city to receive rewards—soldiers may lay down their armor!"

units.zh: 棄仗之聲，振動天地。
units.en: The clatter of discarded weapons shook heaven and earth.
units.literal: The sound of casting away weapons shook heaven and earth.

units.zh: 日午，亂軍畢集，涇州張從賓、邠州康福、河中安彥威皆遁去。
units.en: By midday the mutineers had massed. Zhang Congbin of Jing, Kang Fu of Bin, and An Yanwei of Hezhong all ran.
units.literal: At noon the mutinous armies had all gathered; Zhang Congbin of Jingzhou, Kang Fu of Binzhou, and An Yanwei of Hezhong all fled.

units.zh: 十七日，思同與藥彥稠、萇從簡俱至長安，劉遂雍閉關不內，乃奔潼關。
units.en: On the seventeenth Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and Chang Congjian reached Chang'an, but Liu Suiyong shut the gates against them and they fled toward Tong Pass.
units.literal: On the seventeenth Sitong, together with Yao Yanchou and Chang Congjian, all reached Chang'an; Liu Suiyong closed the passes and would not admit them, and they fled to Tong Pass.

units.zh: 二十二日，潞王至昭應，前鋒執思同來獻。
units.en: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; the van took Sitong and brought him in as prisoner.
units.literal: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; the vanguard seized Sitong and brought him forward as captive.

units.zh: 王謂左右曰：「思同計乖於事，然盡心於所奉，亦可嘉也。」
units.en: The prince told his attendants, "Sitong chose the losing side, but he gave his whole heart to his lord—that still deserves praise."
units.literal: The prince said to those at his side, "Sitong's plans went awry in the affair, yet he gave his whole heart to what he served—that too can be praised."

units.zh: 顧謂趙守鈞曰：「思同爾之故人，可行迓之於路，達予撫慰之意。」
units.en: He said to Zhao Shoujun, "Sitong is your old friend—go meet him on the road and tell him I mean to treat him kindly."
units.literal: He turned to Zhao Shoujun and said, "Sitong is an old friend of yours; you may go meet him on the road and convey my intent to comfort him."

units.zh: 思同至，潞王讓之曰：「賊臣傾我國家，殘害骨肉，非予弟之過。
units.en: When Sitong came up, the Prince of Lu rebuked him: "Traitors have wrecked the realm and hurt the imperial house—that is not my brother's fault.
units.literal: When Sitong arrived the Prince of Lu reproached him, saying, "Traitorous ministers have overturned our state and harmed the imperial kin—that is no fault of your younger brother.

units.zh: 我起兵岐山，蓋誅一二賊臣耳，爾何首鼠兩端，多方誤我，今日之罪，其可逃乎！」
units.en: I marched from Qishan to kill only a handful of villains. Why did you hedge like a cornered rat and lead me astray at every turn? Can you escape punishment today?!"
units.literal: I raised the army at Qishan to execute only one or two traitor ministers; why did you waver like a rat, misleading me in so many ways? Today's guilt—can it be escaped?!"

units.zh: 思同曰：「臣起自行間，受先朝爵命，秉旄仗鉞，累曆重藩，終無顯效以答殊遇。
units.en: Sitong answered, "I came up from the ranks, took titles from the late emperor, bore commander's insignia, and held one great post after another, yet never repaid that grace with any deed worth the name.
units.literal: Sitong said, "Your servant rose from the ranks, received titles from the former court, bore the banner and battle-axe, and successively held great frontier posts, yet in the end had no outstanding achievement to repay extraordinary favor.

units.zh: 臣非不知攀龍附鳳則福多，扶衰救弱則禍速，但恐瞑目之後，無麵見先帝。
units.en: I know perfectly well that siding with the winner brings fortune and backing the loser brings ruin—but when I shut my eyes I could not face the late emperor.
units.literal: Your servant is not unaware that to cling to the rising dragon and phoenix brings many blessings, while to support the declining and save the weak brings swift calamity—but I fear that after I close my eyes I would have no face to meet the late emperor.

units.zh: 釁鼓膏原，縲囚之常分也。」
units.en: War drums and the executioner's field, the captive's proper fate—that is the law of such days."
units.literal: Beating the war drum and smearing the plain with grease, and the bound prisoner's allotted portion—these are the constant rules."

units.zh: 潞王為之改容，徐謂之曰：「且憩歇。」
units.en: The prince's face softened. He said gently, "Rest awhile."
units.literal: The Prince of Lu changed countenance for him and slowly said, "Rest for a while."

units.zh: 潞王欲用之，而楊思權之徒恥見其面，屢啟劉延朗，言「思同不可留，慮失士心。」
units.en: The prince meant to keep him, but Yang Siquan and the others could not bear to look on him. They told Liu Yanlang again and again, "Sitong must not stay or we will lose the army's loyalty."
units.literal: The Prince of Lu wished to employ him, but Yang Siquan and his sort were ashamed to see his face; they repeatedly told Liu Yanlang, saying, "Sitong cannot be kept—we fear losing the soldiers' hearts."

units.zh: 又，潞王入長安時，尹暉盡得思同家財及諸妓女，故尤惡思同，與劉延朗亟言之。
units.en: When the prince entered Chang'an, Yin Hui had plundered Sitong's house and his singing girls, so he hated Sitong all the more and pressed Liu Yanlang to act.
units.literal: Moreover, when the Prince of Lu entered Chang'an, Yin Hui had seized all of Sitong's family wealth and courtesans; therefore he especially hated Sitong and urged Liu Yanlang with him repeatedly.

units.zh: 屬王醉，不待報，殺思同並其子德勝。
units.en: While the prince was drunk they did not wait for orders and killed Sitong and his son Desheng.
units.literal: When the prince was drunk they did not wait for word and killed Sitong together with his son Desheng.

units.zh: 潞王醒，召思同，左右報已誅之矣。
units.en: When the prince woke he called for Sitong; his attendants said the man was already dead.
units.literal: When the Prince of Lu awoke he summoned Sitong; those at his side reported that he had already been executed.

units.zh: 潞王怒延朗，累日嗟惜之。
units.en: The prince raged at Yanlang and mourned the deed for days.
units.literal: The Prince of Lu was angry with Yanlang and for many days sighed in regret.

units.zh: 及漢高祖即位，詔贈侍中。
units.en: When Gaozu of Later Han came to the throne, the court posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When the Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 索自通，字得之，太原清源人也。
units.en: Suo Zitong, courtesy name Dezhi, came from Qingyuan in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Suo Zitong, courtesy name Dezhi, was a native of Qingyuan in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 父繼昭，以自通貴，授國子監祭酒致仕。
units.en: His father Jizhao, through Zitong's rise, was made libationer of the Directorate of Education and retired.
units.literal: His father Jizhao, because Zitong had become eminent, was appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education and retired.

units.zh: 自通少能騎射，嘗於山墅射獵，莊宗鎮太原時，遇之於野，訊其姓名，即補右番廳直軍使。
units.en: As a youth Zitong was skilled in horsemanship and archery. Hunting at a mountain lodge while Zhuangzong held Taiyuan, he met the prince in the field; asked his name, Zhuangzong at once made him an officer of the Right Barracks guard.
units.literal: Zitong in his youth could ride and shoot; once while hunting at a mountain villa, when the Emperor Zhuangzong was stationed at Taiyuan he met him in the wild, asked his name, and at once appointed him to the Right Barracks Direct Army command.

units.zh: 後因從獵，射中走鹿，轉指揮使。
units.en: On a later hunt he brought down a running stag and was promoted to commandant.
units.literal: Later, on a follow hunt he shot a running deer and was transferred to commandant.

units.zh: 佐周德威攻燕軍於涿州，擒燕將郭在鈞。
units.en: He fought under Zhou Dewei against Yan forces at Zhuo and took the Yan general Guo Zaijun.
units.literal: He assisted Zhou Dewei in attacking Yan troops at Zhuozhou and captured the Yan general Guo Zaijun.

units.zh: 從莊宗定魏博，改突騎指揮使。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong in the pacification of Weibo and was made commander of the assault cavalry.
units.literal: He followed the Emperor Zhuangzong in settling Weibo and was changed to commander of the assault cavalry.

units.zh: 明宗即位，自隨駕左右廂馬軍都指揮授忻州刺史。
units.en: When Mingzong succeeded, Zitong left his post as commander of the imperial escort's left and right horse wings to become prefect of Xin.
units.literal: When the Emperor Mingzong took the throne, from his post as commander of the left and right wing horse armies of the imperial escort he was appointed prefect of Xin.

units.zh: 歲餘召還，復典禁兵，領韶州刺史，出為大同軍節度使。
units.en: A year later he was recalled, took the forbidden army again, served as prefect of Shao, and went out as commissioner of Datong.
units.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, again held command of the forbidden troops, held the prefecture of Shao, and went out as military commissioner of Datong.

units.zh: 累歲移鎮忠武，改京兆尹、西京留守。
units.en: He shifted to Zhongwu for several years, then became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.
units.literal: For successive years he was transferred to garrison Zhongwu and was changed to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.

units.zh: 楊彥溫據河中作亂，自通率師討平之，授河中節度使。
units.en: When Yang Yanwen seized Hezhong, Zitong marched against him, crushed the revolt, and was made commissioner of Hezhong.
units.literal: Yang Yanwen held Hezhong in rebellion; Zitong led troops to suppress and pacify him and was appointed military commissioner of Hezhong.

units.zh: 尋自鄜州入為右龍武統軍。
units.en: Soon he left Fuzhou for the capital as commander-in-chief of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
units.literal: Soon after, from Fuzhou he entered court as commander-in-chief of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

units.zh: 初，自通既平楊彥溫，代末帝鎮河中，臨事失於周旋，末帝深銜之。
units.en: After he crushed Yang Yanwen, Zitong replaced the Last Emperor as governor of Hezhong. He handled affairs clumsily, and the Last Emperor nursed a deep grudge.
units.literal: At first, after Zitong had pacified Yang Yanwen he replaced the Last Emperor in garrisoning Hezhong; in handling affairs he was deficient in tact, and the Last Emperor deeply resented him.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：自通至鎮，承安重誨指，籍軍府甲仗數上之，以為從珂私造，賴王德妃居中保護，從珂由是得免。）〉
units.en: (《Comprehensive Mirror》: On reaching his command Zitong followed An Chonghui's orders, counted the arsenal's arms and armor and reported them to court as proof that Congke was forging weapons in secret. Only Consort De's intervention saved Congke from ruin.)〉
units.literal: (《Comprehensive Mirror》: When Zitong reached his post he followed An Chonghui's instructions, inventoried the military stores' arms and armor and reported the count upward, alleging that Congke had privately manufactured them. Thanks to Consort De of Wang's intercession in the middle, Congke thereby escaped harm.)〉

units.zh: 及末帝即位，自通憂悸求死。
units.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, Zitong lived in dread and longed for death.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zitong in fear and dread sought death.

units.zh: 清泰元年七月，因朝退涉洛，自溺而卒。
units.en: In the seventh month of the first year of Qingtai he left court, waded into the Luo, and drowned.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Qingtai, as he withdrew from court he crossed the Luo and drowned himself.

units.zh: 子萬進，周顯德中，曆任方鎮。
units.en: His son Wanjin, under Later Zhou in the Xiande era, held several frontier commands in turn.
units.literal: His son Wanjin, in the Xiande era of Zhou, successively held regional commands.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 以北面行營兵馬都監、鄭州防禦使張虔釗為滄州節度使；
units.en: and Zhang Qianzhao, northern campaign army supervisor and defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, became military governor of Cangzhou;
units.literal: northern campaign horse-army commander-in-chief and Zhengzhou defense commissioner Zhang Qianzhao was made Cang prefecture military commissioner;

units.zh: 有次將劉仁恭者，多權數；
units.en: Among the deputy generals was Liu Rengong, a man of many stratagems.
units.literal: Among the deputy generals was one Liu Rengong, full of stratagems.

units.zh: 攻之彌月不下，乃穴地道以入。
units.en: After a month of siege the city still held, so they dug a tunnel to enter it.
units.literal: They besieged it for a full month without taking it, then dug a tunnel to enter.

units.zh: 時可舉遣將李全忠攻易州。
units.en: Keju then sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.
units.literal: At that time Keju sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.

units.zh: 西京副留守劉遂雍叛降於從珂，思同奔歸於京師，不克，死之。
units.en: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of Luoyang, went over to Congke. Sitong raced for the capital, failed to break through, and was killed.
units.literal: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of the Western Capital, rebelled and surrendered to Congke. Sitong fled back to the capital, could not prevail, and died.

units.zh: 庚申，次長安，西京副留守劉遂雍叛於唐，來降。
units.en: On gengshen he reached Chang’an. Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of Luoyang, broke with the Tang court and submitted.
units.literal: On gengshen he halted at Chang’an. Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of the Western Capital, rebelled against Tang and came to surrender.

units.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使、忠正軍節度使張從賓為涇州節度使，並加檢校太傅；
units.en: Zhang Congbin, commander of the imperial infantry and commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army, was made commissioner of Jingzhou; both were advanced honorary Grand Mentor;
units.literal: Commander of the Imperial Guard infantry, Zhongzheng Army military commissioner Zhang Congbin was made Jingzhou military commissioner, both advanced honorary Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 甲申，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、寧國軍節度使安彥威為河中節度使；
units.en: On jiashen An Yanwei, commander of the imperial cavalry and commissioner of the Ningguo Army, was made commissioner of Hezhong;
units.literal: On jiashen Commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, Ningguo Army military commissioner An Yanwei was made Hezhong military commissioner;

units.zh: 敬瑭懼，幕僚段希堯請誅其倡者，敬瑭命劉知遠斬三十六人以殉。
units.en: Jingtang was afraid; his staff officer Duan Xiyao urged executing the ringleaders; Jingtang ordered Liu Zhiyuan to behead thirty-six men as a warning.
units.literal: Jingtang was afraid; his staff officer Duan Xiyao requested executing the ringleaders; Jingtang ordered Liu Zhiyuan to behead thirty-six men as a warning.

units.zh: 三月丙辰，思同兵潰，嚴衛指揮使尹暉、羽林指揮使楊思權以其軍叛降於從珂。
units.en: On bingchen of the third month Sitong’s force collapsed. Yin Hui of the Yanwei command and Yang Siquan of the Yulin command took their units over to Congke.
units.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, Sitong’s army was routed. Yin Hui, commander of the Yanwei guard, and Yang Siquan, commander of the Yulin guard, led their troops in defection and surrendered to Congke.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 時嗣源遙領鎮州，詰旦，議欲歸藩，上章請罪，安重誨以為不可，語在《明宗紀》中。
units.en: Siyuan still held Zhen at a distance; at dawn he debated returning to his post and asked punishment; An Chonghui forbade it—the account is in the 《Mingzong Annals》.
units.literal: At the time Siyuan held Zhenzhou at a distance; at dawn he debated returning to his circuit and submitted a memorial asking punishment; An Chonghui held it impossible—the account is in the 《Mingzong Annals》.

units.zh: 是月，命開封尹王瓚為北面行營招討使。
units.en: That month Wang Zan, Kaifeng prefect, was named Northern Line pacification commissioner.
units.literal: That month Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan was made Northern Line camp pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 瓚乃與許州留後王彥章等率大軍自黎陽濟，營於楊村，造浮梁以通津路。
units.en: Zan crossed from Liyang with Wang Yanzhang of Xu, camped at Yang village, and bridged the ford.
units.literal: Zan then with Xu retention commissioner Wang Yanzhang and others led a great army across from Liyang, encamped at Yang village, and built a floating bridge to open the crossing.

units.zh: 辛卯，王瓚帥師至戚城，遇晉軍。
units.en: On xinmao, Wang Zan marched to Qi city and encountered the Jin.
units.literal: On xinmao, Wang Zan led troops to Qi city and met Jin troops.

units.zh: 十二月戊戌，晉王領軍迫河南寨，王瓚率師禦之，獲晉將石家才。
units.en: On wuxu in the twelfth month the Prince of Jin pressed the Henan stockade; Wang Zan held him off and took the Jin general Shi Jiacai.
units.literal: On wuxu in the twelfth month, the Prince of Jin led troops to press the Henan stockade; Wang Zan led troops to resist and captured Jin general Shi Jiacai.

units.zh: 既而瓚軍不利，瓚退保楊村寨，晉人陷濮陽。
units.en: Soon Zan was beaten back to Yang village; the Jin seized Puyang.
units.literal: Before long Zan's army met ill fortune; Zan withdrew to defend Yang village stockade, and the Jin took Puyang.

units.zh: 交綏而退。
units.en: After a brief clash both sides drew off.
units.literal: They crossed arms and withdrew.

units.zh: 帝怒，命宋州節度使元行欽率騎三千赴鄴都招撫，詔征諸道之師進討。
units.en: Cunxu sent Yuan Xingqin of Song with 3,000 horse to pacify Ye and ordered circuit armies to attack.
units.literal: The Emperor in rage ordered Songzhou military commissioner Yuan Xingqin to lead three thousand cavalry to Ye to pacify them, and issued an edict the various circuits' armies to advance for punishment.

units.zh: 辛丑，元行欽至鄴都，進攻南門，以詔書招諭城中，趙在禮獻羊酒勞軍，登城遙拜行欽曰：「將士經年離隔父母，不取敕旨歸寧，上貽聖憂，追悔何及！
units.en: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and used an edict to summon the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and bowed from the wall to Xingqin, saying, "The soldiers have been separated from their parents for years; by returning home without edict, they have burdened the sage with worry. What regret can suffice!
units.literal: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and with an edict summoned the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and from the wall bowed distantly to Xingqin, saying, "The troops were separated from parents for years and, not taking the edict to return home, burdened the sage—what regret can suffice!

units.zh: 丁未，鄴都行營招撫使元行欽率諸道之師再攻鄴都。
units.en: On dingwei Yuan Xingqin led circuit armies against Ye again.
units.literal: On dingwei Ye campaign pacification commissioner Yuan Xingqin led the various circuits' armies to attack Ye again.

units.zh: 行欽曰：「上以汝輩有社稷功，必行赦宥。」
units.en: Xingqin said, "Because you have merit for the altars of state, the sovereign will surely grant pardon."
units.literal: Xingqin said, "The sovereign, because you have merit for the altars of state, will surely grant pardon."

units.zh: 行欽以聞，帝怒曰：「收城之日，勿遺噍類！」
units.en: Cunxu, told, raged: "When the city falls, spare none!"
units.literal: Xingqin reported it; the Emperor in rage said, "On the day the city is taken, leave no mouth!"

units.zh: 壬寅，行欽自鄴退軍，保澶州。
units.en: On renyin Xingqin withdrew to Chan.
units.literal: On renyin Xingqin withdrew from Ye and held Chanzhou.

units.zh: 以潁州團練使高行周為安北都護，充振武節度使。
units.en: Gao Xingzhou, Yingzhou training commissioner, became Protector-General of Pacifying the North and Zhenwu commissioner.
units.literal: Yingzhou training commissioner Gao Xingzhou was made Protector-General of Pacifying the North and Zhenwu military commissioner.
